disputes.resolution: fix: Keep the official answer B, confirmed by the question image and tagged bank; no examiner comment is present. In build/work/mcq/overrides.json under 9701_w19_12_q12, set stem to "Which diagram correctly shows the electronegativity of the elements Na, Mg, Al and Si plotted against their first ionisation energies?" and explanation to "B is correct. Electronegativity increases in the order Na < Mg < Al < Si, whereas first ionisation energy increases in the order Na < Al < Mg < Si. Aluminium loses a higher-energy, more shielded 3p electron, which is easier to remove than a 3s electron from magnesium. Therefore Al must be above and to the left of Mg on these axes. A is wrong because it incorrectly places Al at a higher first ionisation energy than Mg.". Preserve answer B and the existing image; the image supplies the graphical options.

findings.evidence: Which type of bonding is never found in elements?
findings.suggested: Replace this item with a question that tests predicting ionic or covalent bonding from Pauling electronegativity differences.
findings.resolution: keep: The finding is incorrect: the bundle explicitly includes this past-paper question under 9701-3.1.4. Identical atoms have zero electronegativity difference, connecting the exclusion of ionic bonding in elemental substances to predicting bond type. B is correct; covalent bonding, metallic bonding and van der Waals forces all occur in elemental substances.
